review_notes: Drafted by Claude, the same assistant building the extraction pipeline this label set will score -- NOT an independent human researcher. Uttam or Abhishek should still spot-check before formally treating this as ground truth. Independent re-check (2026-09-27, via WebFetch/WebSearch against live basecamp.com/37signals.com pages, a separate process from the original drafting and from the extraction pipeline's OpenAI calls): every field confirmed accurate against fresh fetches -- no corrections needed. Two things noted, not changed: (1) traction.certifications lists only PCI DSS; the security page also references a CSA CAIQ v4.1 self-assessment and an EDUCAUSE HECVAT 4 toolkit response, but both are self-assessment questionnaires answered by the company, not certifications issued to it, so they were deliberately left out (same reasoning as bajajauto.json's award-vs-certification distinction). (2) traction.partnerships lists 13 real, confirmed integration partners, but basecamp.com/integrations now lists roughly 80 across 8 categories -- the label's list is a genuine but non-exhaustive subset, not a wrong one. Human review (Uttam, 2026-09-27): checked against the live site independently of the pipeline and of Claude; confirmed as-is, no corrections needed. This satisfies the PRD Section 12 ground-truth requirement.
